findings.title: Missing all-clients resource type resource leads to NullPointerException instead of denial
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no client-specific resource exists, the code loads the 'Clients' resource-type resource via AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(...) and passes the result straight to getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the 'Clients' resource is absent. That happens for any realm whose admin-permissions client was initialized before this change, since the diff adds no migration or lazy creation of the 'Clients' resource and the new scopes. The request then fails with an NPE (HTTP 500) rather than being evaluated as 'no permission'. The same unguarded pattern is in the fallback path of hasPermission(String) only indirectly, but hasPermission(ClientModel, String) is the one that breaks.

findings.title: Listener cleanup for role/client/group removal is now gated on the wrong feature flag
findings.body: The registerListener body is now wrapped in a check on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ. Previously the RoleRemoved, ClientRemoved and GroupRemoved handlers ran unconditionally. This PR does not mention this change, and it is unrelated to the Clients resource type. Realms that use only the V2 feature (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2) and not the V1 flag will no longer have permission records cleaned up when roles, clients or groups are deleted. The GroupRemovedEvent branch is also newly gated, which changes behavior beyond the stated scope. This should be a separate change or the gating should be justified.

findings.title: getResourceName does not map client resources to a readable name
findings.body: getResourceName special-cases the Users type, resolving the user's username for display. The new Clients type has no equivalent branch, so for client-object resources it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). Resources created by resolveClient are named by client UUID and are not given a display name, so the permission UI/API would show a null or raw ID for client permissions. A Clients branch that resolves the client's clientId, mirroring the Users branch, is needed.

findings.title: requireView() javadoc describes the wrong behavior
findings.body: The javadoc for requireView() says 'Returns true if canView() returns true', but the method returns void and is meant to throw ForbiddenException when canView() is false. The doc should say it throws. The same copy-paste error appears in the requireViewClientScopes() javadoc at line 103.

findings.title: canList() javadoc references QUERY_USERS for client listing
findings.body: The canList() javadoc says it returns true if the caller has QUERY_CLIENTS or QUERY_USERS. For a client-listing predicate, QUERY_USERS looks like a copy-paste from the user evaluator. Either the doc or the implementation is wrong, and the contract should be checked against the implementation.
